correctness.rationale: Orthogonal bimedian decomposition yields the four sign-pattern vertices (±a,±b,±c) with even minus parity. A central Haar plane generically separates vertices 1+3 or 2+2; spherical sign correlation E(sgn(u·v_i)sgn(u·v_j))=1-2θ_ij/π yields q=3-(4/π)Σarcsin√p_i. Fix t=max p_i and split p2+p3=1-t under p2,p3≤t. Strict concavity of f(x)=arcsin√x for x<1/2 makes the minimum q occur at p2=p3=(1-t)/2 and the maximal q at (t,1-2t) for t<1/2, else approach p3→0 giving q→1. The inverse intervals and t=1/2 geometry follow. Independently simulated 240,000 Haar normals over three shapes and checked 1,200 random conditional triples; analytic proof, not sampling, establishes the continuum theorem.
